In terms of its operation, it provides financial institutions with a one-stop mutual learning platform to acquire the knowledge, tools and information needed to formulate their own green finance roadmaps and transform into credible green financial institutions; brings together green finance leaders and connects green financial institutions across different emerging markets to promote communication and explore frontier issues; and advances the global green finance agenda, unlocking boundless green and climate-related investment opportunities. In June, five globally leading financial institutions5 became founding members of the Alliance and worked closely with the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA to encourage clients to adopt green strategies, promote best practices for green products and services, and unlock new business opportunities that help realise the green economic transition. In addition, three global partners and one knowledge partner6 committed in 2022 to providing climate expertise in areas ranging from innovation and standardisation to academic research. Details of the Alliance and its membership structure are available on the relevant webpage (English version): Founding members, and the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA signing the Memorandum of Understanding. On the other hand, since March 2021 the Alliance has held 18 training events and roundtable meetings, attracting more than 6,000 participants from around the world, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. Furthermore, in June 2022 the Alliance, together with the Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (the Institute)7, published its first frontier-issue research report entitled "Climate Risk: Definition, Measurement, Current Practices and Regulation". The HKMA has been promoting the issuance of green and sustainable debt and cultivating an ecosystem of related professional services locally. The total amount of green and sustainable debt (including bonds and loans) issued in Hong Kong in 2022 reached US$80.5 billion, an increase of 42%. +42% Green and sustainable debt issuance (US$80.5 billion). To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and commit to developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018, with the HKMA assisting in the issuance of the relevant green bonds. To date, the Government has issued green institutional and retail bonds equivalent to nearly US$16 billion, with the proceeds allocated to more than 40 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the programme, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report" detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. To allow members of the public to participate in Hong Kong's sustainable development through investment and share in the resulting benefits, the first batch of green retail bonds with a total value of HK$20 billion was issued in May, receiving enthusiastic support from the public and becoming the largest green retail bond issuance in the world at the time. This issuance also expanded the range of green and sustainable finance products in Hong Kong, consolidating Hong Kong's position as a premier green finance hub in the region and internationally. The Government also continued its regular green institutional bond issuance work in the 2022–23 financial year, and in January 2023 issued green bonds equivalent to US$5.75 billion. This tri-currency issuance covered the US dollar, euro and renminbi, with tenors ranging from 2 to 30 years, continuing to provide an important benchmark for potential issuers in Hong Kong and the region. This issuance was widely welcomed by the global investment community and successfully attracted new investors who had not participated in the Government's previous green bond issuances, reflecting investors' confidence in Hong Kong's long-term credit standing and economic fundamentals. In response to investor demand, the Government doubled the issuance size of the renminbi bonds to RMB10 billion. The share of international investors and Mainland investors participating in this issuance through Bond Connect's "Southbound Trading" also increased, demonstrating Hong Kong's position as the premier offshore renminbi business hub and further consolidating Hong Kong's leading position as an international financial centre. In February 2023, the HKMA also assisted the Government in issuing tokenised green institutional bonds to test the use of distributed ledger technology for bond issuance and settlement. These were the world's first tokenised green bonds issued by a government. This primary issuance was settled on a T+1 basis on a private blockchain network, and the subsequent processes (including coupon payment, secondary market trading settlement and redemption at maturity) were also digitalised. The Government's experience in this issuance can serve as a reference for market participants interested in conducting similar bond issuances in the future. To provide the industry with credible and convenient market information, the HKMA continued to collaborate with the Climate Bonds Initiative and the International Capital Market Association to publish annual reports on the green debt markets in Hong Kong and the region respectively. The International Capital Market Association's report showed that in 2022 Hong Kong became the largest hub in Asia for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds, with the total amount of bonds arranged through Hong Kong reaching US$27.8 billion, accounting for more than one-third of the regional total. The largest arranging hub for international green and sustainable bonds in Asia, US$27.8 billion. Following its first issuance in 2021, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued another RMB5 billion of offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong in November 2022, including RMB2.6 billion of green and blue bonds8. In the same month, the People's Government of Hainan Province also issued RMB5 billion of offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, including blue and sustainable bonds. The above bond issuance activities once again highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world, as well as its enduring position as the premier fund-raising platform in the region. The HKMA continued to promote and implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" launched in 2021, and used the scheme to attract more relevant professional service providers (including financial institutions, green advisory firms and external review agencies) to establish and expand their businesses in Hong Kong. The scheme has been widely welcomed by the industry. As at the end of 2022, the scheme had covered the pre-issuance, post-issuance or both external review service expenses of issuers of more than 180 green and sustainable debt instruments, helping issuers ensure and demonstrate strict adherence to market best practices and international standards. From March, the scheme was enhanced by lowering the minimum loan size threshold for applying for external review fee subsidies from HK$200 million to HK$100 million, helping smaller enterprises obtain green financing. Following the successful completion of the proof-of-concept for tokenised retail green bonds under Project Genesis in 2021, the HKMA collaborated again with the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre under Genesis 2.0 to explore the technical feasibility of digitalised carbon forwards (also known as mitigation outcome interests, or MOIs), thereby enhancing the transparency, objectivity and environmental credentials of the green bond market. The project was completed in October 2022, successfully developing two prototypes that use blockchain and other related technologies to track, deliver and transfer digitalised MOIs.

As one of the world's largest asset owners and managers, the HKMA plays an important role in promoting the development of green and sustainable finance to support the global climate change agenda. The HKMA is also a pioneer in responsible investment, having taken the lead in investing in green and sustainable assets as early as 2015, requiring its external investment managers to adopt the Principles of Responsible Ownership issued by the Securities and Futures Commission, and integrating environmental, social and governance factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term value enhancement", believing that placing importance on environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors can unlock long-term sustainable value for investments and mitigate related risks. Facing the increasingly severe challenges of climate change, the HKMA continues to advance on its responsible investment journey, including setting a "Net Zero by 2050" target in 2022 and enhancing its risk management strategy, thereby strengthening the resilience of its asset portfolio to achieve more favourable long-term risk-adjusted returns for the Exchange Fund. The HKMA also actively participates in building a green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors and regulators to jointly promote responsible investment, and collaborating with international organisations to develop ESG investment standards. The transparency of climate-related information plays a pivotal role in managing climate risks. To fulfil its commitment in support of the Glasgow Declaration issued by the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) at the 2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference and to greening the global financial system, the HKMA makes climate-related disclosures on the Exchange Fund in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) under the Financial Stability Board. a. FCLTGlobal — Focusing Capital on the Long Term b. PRI — Principles for Responsible Investment c. NGFS — Network for Greening the Financial System d. TCFD — Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The foremost guiding principle is for the HKMA to give priority to ESG investments whose long-term risk-adjusted returns are comparable to those of other projects, so as to fulfil the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Details of the HKMA's responsible investment framework are set out on the HKMA website: The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors the progress of integrating ESG factors into investments as well as the ESG position of the Exchange Fund through regular meeting reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Department of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 1, the ESG Committee established under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring the various ESG efforts of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The matters discussed and the progress of work at each meeting of the ESG Committee are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Monitoring and Governance Structure of Responsible Investment The dedicated teams of the Risk Management and Compliance Department work closely with the various investment teams of the Exchange Fund Investment Office on the integration of ESG factors, and assist the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the ESG and climate-related risks and opportunities of various investments: Public Market Investments The Credit, Compliance and Monitoring Committee, comprising the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, monitors the ESG position of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reporting from the Risk Management and Compliance Department. In addition, the Risk Management and Compliance Department also participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring process of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see the section "Striving to Actively Exercise Asset Ownership" under the "Risk Management" section on page 27). Private Market Investments The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the Risk Management and Compliance Department and the private market investment teams on each investment proposal. Concrete evidence² continues to show that the impacts of climate change and related risks are significant. According to the latest report³ of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (the Framework Convention), even assuming the full implementation of the "Nationally Determined Contributions" targets announced by various regions, the global temperature rise by 2100 is still estimated to reach as high as 2.1 to 2.4 degrees Celsius, making it difficult to achieve the goal of the Paris Agreement to limit the increase in the global average temperature to below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. If various regions adopt more aggressive policy measures to narrow the temperature gap, the resulting transition risks⁴, along with the repricing of assets by the market based on anticipated future trends, coupled with inherent physical risks, would all intensify the pressure on asset valuations. In view of the updated global warming trajectory and model assumptions, the HKMA, leveraging the expertise of external consultants, further assessed the resilience of the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" under the "Rapid Transition" scenario (Figure 2), in addition to the scenarios assessed in 2021. The "Rapid Transition" scenario incorporates higher transition risk factors in the short, medium and long term, assuming that policy changes and technological developments jointly drive a rapid decline in carbon emissions, while various assets would be suddenly divested to keep the average temperature rise within 1.5 degrees Celsius before 2100. This scenario is broadly consistent with the disorderly scenario recommended by the NGFS for forward-looking climate impact assessments. The "Investment Portfolio" is able to remain robust over the medium to long term, as a relatively large proportion of its asset allocation consists of sovereign bonds that are less sensitive to transition impacts. The sector distribution is key. Low-carbon electricity and renewable energy assets can benefit from the relevant transition. Transition risks and asset repricing may impact performance (especially equity assets) in the short term. The "Investment Portfolio" as a whole would be increasingly affected by physical risks that gradually emerge over time. Energy and traditional utilities remain the most vulnerable sectors. Climate scenarios, like other model-based approaches, have their limitations. The analysis is based on the sector distribution of market benchmarks at the strategic asset allocation level, and does not take into account the effect of actively selecting specific securities within a particular sector. In-depth research reveals that the investments within the "Investment Portfolio" are generally more resilient to transition shocks or less affected compared with the market benchmarks of the strategic asset allocation. This result reaffirms that the HKMA's responsible investment, with a focus on combating climate change, can enhance the resilience of the asset portfolio. The trajectory of climate change remains uncertain, and scenario analysis methods will continue to evolve as data quality improves and policies develop. The HKMA will regularly review relevant scenarios and refine its assessments to more clearly ascertain the resilience of the Exchange Fund in the face of climate change. As a long-term investor, the HKMA fully understands the risks and opportunities that climate change may bring. The HKMA is committed to further expanding sustainable investment and seizing opportunities related to climate transition, mitigating climate risks and enhancing the long-term returns of its asset portfolio. In 2022, the HKMA continued its strong momentum, increasing its holdings of green, social and sustainable bonds by a further 50%. In terms of equity investments, the HKMA invested in an actively managed equity portfolio with a governance theme, and adopted a decarbonisation strategy that tilts towards low-carbon-emission companies for its passive equity portfolio. In addition, the HKMA is exploring with the dedicated general partner of the Exchange Fund's "Long-Term Growth Portfolio" the establishment of a dedicated private equity portfolio to promote green and sustainable development in Asia (Figure 3). Figure 3 Ongoing Measures to Increase ESG Investment The HKMA has invested in a pan-African wind farm operator which, in addition to producing clean energy, also places great importance on social and biodiversity factors. Before the wind farm was established, local villagers used poisoned bait to prevent predatory animals from preying on their livestock, but this inadvertently endangered certain vultures that are endangered species. Livestock is an important asset for the local villagers, and to help them protect their livestock, the operator built livestock shelters within the wind farm to protect the livestock from natural predators. In addition, the operator employed a bird monitoring team to issue warnings when vultures were found being attracted by animal carcasses occasionally left behind by predators, so as to shut down the wind turbines and prevent the vultures from being struck by the blades. Reducing livestock predation created a win-win situation: on the one hand, it safeguarded the livelihoods of the villagers, and on the other hand, it reduced the number of vultures killed by being struck by wind turbines, thereby protecting endangered species. Good ESG practices can bring more business opportunities to enterprises and open up new revenue streams, as illustrated by the following supply-chain-related operation. The investee company is an integrated logistics and warehousing operator in Mainland China, specialising in cold-chain logistics services for pharmaceuticals, chemical products and high-end consumer goods. The company faces continuously rising ESG operating standards, primarily driven by multinational enterprise clients requiring their service providers to achieve ambitious decarbonisation targets in line with the Paris Agreement. In response to such demand, the company engaged external consultants to help formulate a "Three-Year ESG Plan" to reduce carbon emission intensity by 50% by 2030 or earlier. This comprehensive decarbonisation plan delivered significant results in 2021 alone. The above ESG measures earned the company the "Low-Carbon Green Management Case" award from the China Federation of Logistics and Purchasing. These achievements and accolades have enabled the company to gain considerable business opportunities from multinational corporate clients in the consumer and chemical products sectors that place particular emphasis on ESG practices. The growth of ESG investment is closely linked to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry skills. In 2022, the HKMA successfully held its 4th annual ESG workshop, exchanging good ESG practices with 9 participating private market institutions (including general partners, limited partners and enterprises), and promoting sustainable investment opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. On the public market side, the HKMA urged its trading counterparties (mainly investment banks) to expand their ESG manpower and research capabilities, particularly in Hong Kong. Mr Howard Lee, Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, delivering the opening remarks at the HKMA ESG Workshop 2022. At the international level, the HKMA actively participates in the work of setting industry ESG investment standards and practices: As one of the earliest central bank signatories to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA participated in the joint action of signatories coordinated by the PRI to develop a standardised responsible investment due diligence questionnaire for private equity and venture capital investments⁵,⁶, to assist private market investors in conducting ESG assessments of general partners and investment proposals. The HKMA participated in several working groups to support the research work of FCLTGlobal; this research aims to explore the market's key practices for long-term investment portfolios and for decarbonising private assets, as well as the application of such practices to long-term investors. As a member of the NGFS and a supporter of the TCFD, the HKMA contributed to the NGFS's "Guide on Climate-related Disclosure for Central Banks" to demonstrate its commitment to adopting good ESG practices. The HKMA also led a working group under the NGFS's "Net Zero for Central Banks" workstream, participating in the development of sustainable and responsible investment approaches for the central banking community. The HKMA continues to participate in various industry forums and seminars to share insights on responsible investment and climate change strategies. Ms Vanessa Lau, Chief Risk Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office (centre), speaking at a sharing session on ESG investment opportunities. Building internal capacity is crucial for continuing to advance on the ESG journey. In addition to encouraging staff to pursue courses related to sustainable development and to obtain relevant qualifications, the HKMA has also gained relevant knowledge and practical experience from the process in 2021 in which external consultants provided advice on the industry's key practices for the climate transition of the asset portfolio. On the other hand, the HKMA also uses ESG data compiled by reputable external information providers to complement its ongoing analysis of the asset portfolio, so as to help strengthen the ESG resilience of the Exchange Fund.

The HKMA is committed to reducing the carbon footprint of its own organisation, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and contributing to Hong Kong's overall climate targets. While striving to promote environmental sustainability, the HKMA also fulfils its commitments to caring for the physical and mental well-being of its staff, encouraging financial inclusion, and discharging its social responsibilities. The HKMA is dedicated to conducting its day-to-day operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. To this end, the HKMA puts sustainable development into practice under the three pillars of environment, staff, and social responsibility (Diagram 1). The Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating and implementing its sustainability strategy. The Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with members including three Deputy Chief Executives, as well as representatives from the Risk Management and Surveillance Department and the Corporate Development and Operations Department; it submits regular reports to the Governance Sub-Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee. Under the leadership of this Committee, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing measures within their respective areas. In 2022, the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee approved the climate targets for the organisation's operations and reviewed the transition roadmap for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the Committee continued to review the progress of the HKMA's green measures, including recommendations to strengthen the HKMA's sustainable procurement policies, procedures, and methodologies. Governance Structure for Sustainability HKMA's Corporate Sustainability Journey In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service presented the HKMA with the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for the 16th consecutive year. The HKMA pays great attention to the carbon footprint of its own organisation and has established internal "Green Office Guidelines" to manage the environmental impact of its operational procedures. The HKMA has integrated environmental factors into the interior design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. In 2022, BEAM Plus awarded the HKMA a Gold rating for certain renovated office areas. This was the second green building certification obtained, following the LEED Gold certification received in 2021. Awarded BEAM Plus Interiors Version 1.0 Gold The HKMA has implemented a number of energy-saving measures. Total energy consumption in 2022⁶ was 4,996.4 megawatt-hours (2.8 megawatt-hours per person⁷), a decrease of 24.4% compared with 2015 (Figure 1). Total Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions in 2022⁸ amounted to 2,996.4 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per person), a decrease of 38.2% compared with 2015 (Figure 2). Figure 1 Figure 2 Greenhouse Gas Emissions Intensity (Scope 1 and 2) The HKMA encourages paperless operations within the organisation. In addition, the HKMA has implemented a print management system, requiring staff to log in at the printer to confirm each printing request, which helps reduce unnecessary printouts and toner usage. When printing is genuinely necessary, double-sided printing and black-and-white printing are also encouraged. The HKMA is also preparing to implement an internal electronic recordkeeping system. Total paper consumption in 2022 was 20.5 tonnes (0.0114 tonnes per person), a decrease of 65.3% compared with 2015 (Figure A). Figure A: Paper Intensity The HKMA continues to adhere to the "4R" principle in its waste management efforts. In addition to conventional waste, the HKMA also reduces electronic waste by adopting technological solutions such as server virtualisation and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external firm for the first time to conduct a waste audit, analysing the composition of waste generated in the office. The audit found that food waste accounted for a large portion of the total waste, prompting the HKMA to launch a food waste recycling programme (see "Strengthening Waste Management" on page 41). Total non-hazardous waste generated in 2022 (including general refuse and recyclables) was 242.0 tonnes (0.135 tonnes per person), a decrease of 4.8% compared with 2015 (Figure 3). The fluctuation in the trend was mainly due to the work-from-home arrangements implemented during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and the resumption of office operations after the fifth wave of the pandemic. Figure 3 Non-Hazardous Waste Intensity The HKMA places top priority on waste reduction at source, and is committed to reducing, reusing, and recycling. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit, in order to gain a clearer understanding of the composition of waste (plastics, paper, metal, glass, wood, electronics, etc.) generated in daily operations, and to provide recommendations for waste reduction. Based on the results of this audit, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, placing food waste collection bins in all pantries. The food waste collected each day is transported to an organic resources recovery centre in Hong Kong, where it is converted into renewable energy for electricity generation. The residues produced during the conversion process can also be made into compost for use in landscaping and agricultural production. In addition, recycling bins are placed at various locations in the office for convenience. The HKMA shares recycling tips with staff, and pays greater attention to further improving the source separation of recyclables, as well as the points to note when handling recyclables such as cartons, food containers, and beverage bottles. In addition, we continue to organise activities to raise staff's environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage staff to make good use of the recycling facilities within the office. Food waste collected each day is transported to an organic resources recovery centre Recycled plastic items The HKMA operates two data centres (one operational and one backup). As they account for a major portion of the organisation's overall energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green design and a number of energy-saving measures, including rack-based air-conditioning systems, LED lighting, and round-the-clock monitoring of power efficiency. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of the aforementioned data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to improve overall energy efficiency. It has also begun preparations for obtaining green data centre certification. The HKMA recognises the importance of building a culture of sustainability, and therefore regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage staff to develop habits conducive to sustainability and to adopt green and digital ways of working. The HKMA shares green living tips with staff, as well as annual office-wide energy and paper consumption statistics, reminding them to help address environmental issues at a personal level; it also encourages staff to put forward suggestions on sustainability matters. Led by a Senior Manager of the Administration Division, a task force brings together staff from different departments to brainstorm and put forward ideas and concrete measures to promote a green working environment. Members of the task force also serve as ambassadors when new green measures are rolled out. The HKMA encourages the wider community to adopt more environmentally friendly practices, and has launched a number of measures to improve the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry, and the economy as a whole, so as to minimise resource consumption. The HKMA's Submission Through Electronic Transmission (STET) system is a one-stop platform that allows banks to submit documents to the HKMA electronically, covering various types of periodic returns required on a weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annual basis. Another system, e-Delivery, is a secure electronic communication channel that enables the HKMA to issue information such as circulars and guidelines to banks. Both systems help save large amounts of paper each year. In handling bank complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken measures to support paperless submission of documents, with bank customers able to lodge complaints through electronic channels and by completing online forms. The HKMA is also developing a new-generation management information system to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper records to digital records. To reduce paper usage, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU)⁹ has adopted digital signatures in its day-to-day communications with its members, including in issuing circulars, account opening and account termination letters, and in responding to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore more green measures, including the adoption of automated electronic processes for internal and external communications. The HKMA encourages the public to make greater use of electronic payment methods in place of cash and physical cheques by promoting the use of the Faster Payment System (FPS) and stored value facilities. Further information on FPS and stored value facilities can be found in the chapter "Hong Kong as an International Financial Centre" of the HKMA Annual Report 2022. Distributing e-lai see is simple and convenient, and reduces the use of physical red packets and banknotes, helping to promote sustainability in Hong Kong. To this end, the HKMA continued to actively promote e-lai see across various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to distribute e-lai see via online or mobile banking services using FPS or other e-wallet services during the Lunar New Year. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organised various activities to attract users to use e-lai see, such as offering user interfaces with a festive Lunar New Year atmosphere, enhancing functions to make usage more convenient, and launching lucky draws or cash rebates. The HKMA promoted e-lai see on social media platforms For members of the public who choose to distribute physical lai see during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continued to encourage them to use "good-as-new" banknotes—that is, banknotes that are used but still look fresh—for their lai see. Good-as-new banknotes can reduce the need to print new banknotes, thereby lessening the impact on the environment. Feedback from note-issuing banks shows that the public has become increasingly receptive to good-as-new banknotes in recent years. The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA's efforts to promote coin recycling. The coins collected through the programme are returned to the market to meet public demand, improving the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need to mint new coins. The programme comprises two Coin Carts, which have to date recorded more than 1 million uses and collected over 800 million coins with a total face value of about HK$1.3 billion. In 2022, about 78% of users chose to use part or all of their coin value to top up their stored value facility accounts. The HKMA has been working with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying Coin Carts to collect coins on NGO flag days, in an effort to support social services. The coin-counting machine on the Coin Cart The Coin Collection Programme was launched in 2014 and was the world's first systematic coin collection programme to adopt the mobile-cart concept. Over the years, it has received numerous local and international awards, in recognition of its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin handling. The programme comprises two Coin Carts, each equipped with two high-speed coin-counting machines to collect the coins exchanged by the public. Members of the public may choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, use them to top up stored value facility (such as Octopus card or e-wallet) accounts, or donate them to the Community Chest for charity. In addition to collecting coins, the Coin Carts are also deployed from time to time for various educational activities (such as student visits).

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency ("HKQAA") conducted an independent verification of the climate targets ("Climate Targets") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Climate Targets were established with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual ("SBTi Corporate Manual"). The purpose of this verification exercise was to verify whether the Climate Targets were established with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. This verification exercise was carried out in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusion in order to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the data. Our verification work was fully independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes: • The Climate Targets were established with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Sum Siu-yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023.  Verification Statement: The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency ("HKQAA") conducted an independent verification of the 2022 environmental data ("2022 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2022 Data includes the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emission intensity, paper consumption intensity, non-hazardous waste generation intensity and recycling rate for 2022, as well as the changes in this data compared with 2015 levels. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emission data was compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly issued by the World Resources Institute ("WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development ("WBCSD"). The scope of verification covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, and also covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison. The scope of verification covers a total of 6 office and warehouse assets: 4 offices at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 2 warehouses at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre and 6) Sunley Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan respectively. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification exercise was carried out in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusion in order to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data back to its source, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checks, and conducted reliability testing. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the data. Our verification work was fully independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the process of preparing the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the 2022 Data and concludes: • The 2022 Data is substantially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Sum Siu-yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023.

Scaling up and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing issue of our time. We are already almost halfway through this critical decade for the climate crisis. We need to cut global carbon emissions by more than 40% within this decade to have any hope of limiting global warming to within 1.5 degrees Celsius. Yet greenhouse gas emissions keep hitting record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window to keep the global temperature rise within 1.5 degrees Celsius is fast closing. Everyone can already clearly feel the impact of a 1.1-degree Celsius rise in temperature—record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding and storms, and other extreme weather events are occurring more frequently across the globe, each more severe than the last. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, after being battered by a fierce super typhoon, we were immediately met with a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our excellent infrastructure and our ability to respond swiftly to disasters, the impact was still very serious—widespread flooding, disrupted traffic, and damage to roads in numerous locations. All of this serves as a clear reminder that decisive and proactive climate action is truly a matter of the utmost urgency.  Asia faces particularly great challenges on the road to a low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that can appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means an easy task. Owing to the region's rapid economic development and fast population growth, its carbon emissions account for more than half of the global total. At the same time, the Asia-Pacific region is densely populated, and due to its geographical location, it is also vulnerable to rising sea levels and extreme weather. As the region's economies are at different stages of development, the low-carbon transition may bring new opportunities to some economies, but for others, raising the funds needed for the transition is an enormous challenge. The market estimates that the Asia-Pacific region will require more than US$3 trillion in low-carbon transition investment each year over the next 30 years.  As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the capability and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across the whole of Asia. As a banking regulator, a market facilitator, and a responsible investor, the HKMA has consistently devoted significant effort to the sustainability agenda. Readers will learn from the various chapters of this report about the specific measures and initiatives the HKMA has undertaken over the past year. In addition, to strengthen the HKMA's internal governance structure and to coordinate sustainability work across different functional areas more effectively, we established the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee last year. For detailed information on this Steering Committee, please refer to the newly added chapter on "Governance of Sustainability."  Hong Kong's banks play an important role in supporting Asia's transition to net-zero emissions. In addition to fulfilling our traditional function as a banking regulator—ensuring in our day-to-day supervisory work that banks properly manage climate risks—we also play the role of a facilitator, supporting the banking industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green classification framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype of the green classification framework in May for consultation, and we are now refining the framework based on the feedback collected during the consultation period. Moreover, as there is growing demand from all sectors for higher-quality and more globally comparable sustainability disclosure information, the HKMA, together with other regulators, is developing a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards launched by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June—a comprehensive global baseline for sustainability reporting.  The HKMA's role as a facilitator is not limited to developing frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing the pain points faced by the industry. At present, many banks are constrained by data and find it difficult to conduct physical risk assessments. In view of this, the HKMA will shortly launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform. Banks need only enter a property address to assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, thereby helping banks manage the related climate risks.  As a leading international financial centre in Asia and a sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has long served as a bridge, channelling international investment into sustainable development projects in Asia and supporting the region's low-carbon transition. In recent years, the total amount of international green and sustainable bonds arranged and issued in Hong Kong has accounted for more than one-third of the Asian market, clearly leading other regions. Of particular note, the Shenzhen Municipal Government and the Hainan Provincial Government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong in 2023 for the third and second consecutive year respectively, once again affirming Hong Kong's important role as a green gateway connecting the Mainland with the rest of the world. The vibrant development of Hong Kong's sustainable bond activities is partly attributable to the demonstration effect of the "Government Green Bond Programme." Since 2019, the HKMA has helped the Government issue about US$25 billion worth of green bonds, sold to institutional and retail investors. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest government retail green bond in 2022, we issued the world's first batch of tokenised government green bonds in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the issuance of a second batch of tokenised green bonds; denominated in four major currencies and issued in digitally native form, these were the world's first multi-currency digital green bonds.  At the same time, we have also proactively introduced various measures to enhance the vibrancy and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. This covers work in multiple areas such as skills training, improving data, green fintech, and transition finance. In particular, in terms of talent development, in 2023 we introduced a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the banking professional qualification framework, providing bank practitioners with a systematic course to enhance their understanding and expertise in green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key area of our work; it provides funding for the decarbonisation activities of high-carbon-emitting and hard-to-abate industries, so as to prevent these industries from being unable to transition due to a lack of financial support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong's green classification framework to cover transition activities. We will also expand the coverage of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme," which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, in order to encourage enterprises in the region to raise transition funds in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen communication and engagement with relevant stakeholders, attracting private-sector investment in sustainable development projects that have historically been harder to finance, through public-private cooperation and blended finance models.  Some of the above work requires cross-sectoral collaboration, and is mainly coordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, which is co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-standing collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks," the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the "Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment" and the "Green Investment and Financing Partnership" as a founding member in 2023. In addition, the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero" has also announced plans to establish a chapter in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we hope to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, and thereby support channelling funds into sustainable development projects both within the region and around the world.  To drive new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped host the inaugural "Hong Kong Green Week" earlier this year, attracting a total of more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including top decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, to jointly discuss solutions for scaling up climate financing in the region and to forge new partnerships in this regard. Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue delivered a speech at the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum," a flagship event of "Hong Kong Green Week."  As the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a significant asset owner globally, the HKMA leads by example in being a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been at the forefront of green and sustainable asset investment, and has gradually expanded the Exchange Fund's ESG and green asset portfolios in both public and private markets. With regard to the target for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA last year added an active global equity portfolio themed on sustainability and climate transition, while also expanding the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another public-market asset portfolio. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds that the HKMA has prioritised for investment have outperformed their investment benchmarks, embodying the proposition of "doing well by doing good." On the private-market side, we have continued to pursue green-related investment opportunities and became an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. At the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio was 6% and 46% lower than the 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and has consistently been below the overall market level.  As a sustainability-focused institution, the HKMA will continue to strive for improvement, formulating our sustainability goals and plans on the basis of the three pillars of the environment, our staff, and social responsibility. Specifically, on the HKMA's low-carbon transition journey, we continuously strengthen our capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emission reduction, improving energy efficiency, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of fulfilling our commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have already drawn up plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the short term, and have made good progress towards our medium-term target of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain outstanding talent to fulfil the HKMA's various important functions, beyond our green goals, the HKMA is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of our staff. In addition, by working with stakeholders, we promote financial inclusion, enhance the public's level of financial literacy, and raise public awareness of guarding against financial fraud, thereby contributing to the building of a caring society.  The climate challenge is enormous and exceptionally urgent. Economies around the world are moving towards a more sustainable future, and this process is expected to bring about tremendous changes in financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries considerable risks, but it will also be accompanied by unprecedented opportunities. As a leading global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has the responsibility to take the lead in acting to address these challenges. At the same time, we are also well positioned to seize the momentum and rise to the occasion. The HKMA will fully support the industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition; and will continue, as a responsible investor and a sustainable institution, to lead by example and to work with like-minded partners to advance this global agenda that is of the utmost importance at present.  Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are of global concern. The HKMA's goal in its sustainability work is to strive to play a leadership role through its own policies and operations, to ensure that Hong Kong's financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to the risks of climate change, and to support the transition to a more sustainable economic development. Through active participation in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also strive to contribute to the formulation of regional and global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As the banking regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking industry's climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, the key priorities include: launching a new round of thematic examinations on banks' climate risk management practices, and conducting a new round of consultation sessions, as part of reviewing banks' progress in implementing the climate risk management supervisory requirements; continuing the work on incorporating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; completing the second round of the industry-wide climate risk stress test, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing the observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainability disclosures, including working with relevant local authorities to align the relevant requirements with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards, which serve as the global baseline, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Pillar 3 framework on climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance on best practices in transition planning with the industry. To promote the healthy development of banks in offering green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to keep pace with local and international market and regulatory developments, and maintain communication with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate selling processes. In addition, the HKMA will also play the role of a facilitator, striving to promote the development of the green finance ecosystem and to support banks in providing financing for the economic transition. We will soon publish the local green classification framework and continue to expand its coverage to encompass more activities, including transition activities. At the same time, we will also continue to explore the application of technological solutions to help banks identify, measure and monitor their climate risk exposures; one example is the cloud-based platform to be launched soon, which will facilitate banks' physical risk assessments. To enhance the professional competencies of practitioners, in 2024 we will also develop the Professional Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Enhanced Competency Framework for Bank Practitioners". Hong Kong is well positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the proposals in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope of the "Government Green Bond Programme" to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market; at the same time, through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme", it aims to attract more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong. We will also continue to encourage more governments, organisations and enterprises to raise green funds through Hong Kong, and to explore the potential synergies between green finance and technology. In addition, we will continue to assist in implementing the government-funded "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme" to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. As co-chairs of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group" (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and work to promote the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Group will focus its work on three areas, including sustainability disclosures, the application of technology, and transition finance. As another work priority, through the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks", the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various initiatives in the Asian region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training for banks, and providing practical guidance to help banks support financial institutions in establishing their tailored green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our cooperation with the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero", the "Coalition for Climate Resilient Investment" and the "Green Investment and Financing Partnership". As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving the net-zero emissions target for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring that the resilience of the asset portfolio is maintained on the path towards net zero. We fully understand that only by achieving an economy-wide transition can the goals of the "Paris Agreement" be attained, and therefore we are optimising our net-zero strategy, focusing on assets that can bring positive climate benefits to the real economy, while taking into account the Exchange Fund's investment objectives. As an environmentally supportive institution, the HKMA's decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest market, regulatory, technological and other climate-related developments. To further strengthen the HKMA's climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technological solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage staff to participate in our sustainability work, including launching campaigns to cultivate sustainable habits and optimising office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices when selecting and renewing contracts. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the designated certification standards. In terms of the regular upgrades of the data centre facilities, in addition to keeping pace with the latest technological developments, we will also incorporate green design and practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, and actively modernise internal systems to enhance efficiency and minimise potential risks as far as possible. Finally, in terms of the social focus area, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for its colleagues, and work with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, as well as to raise public awareness of guarding against financial fraud.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. The HKMA, through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor and sustainable development organisation, contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework that leads the formulation of the HKMA's relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of relevant measures, and ensures that sustainability factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and working practices. In its commitment to good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework for its sustainability-related work, featuring clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively incorporated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and it is equipped with effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainability efforts. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which are responsible for overseeing the HKMA's work—including its sustainability efforts—and making recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; on the responsible investment front, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and, with respect to other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), jointly initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's various sustainability efforts over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas.1 It provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of banking, market development, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; assesses the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and oversees the external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. In addition, we invite the responsible Assistant Chief Executives of key functions relating to green and sustainability matters to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on the major outcomes of, and future plans for, their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Department and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA, together with the SFC, initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020.2 As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts relating to the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, in order to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been dedicated to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are exposed to the impacts of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their day-to-day business operations. To continue performing their vital functions in the financial system and to channel more funding towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capabilities to address and manage climate risks, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is committed to formulating various policy measures to strengthen the banking system's ability to address climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to help banks maintain safety and soundness during the process of transitioning the economy to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of the circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey of selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices on transition planning with the industry, and will organise seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experience within the industry.  Regarding disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments—including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards published in June, as well as the consultation launched by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) in November on the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks—the HKMA is stepping up its efforts to enhance the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is working with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that aligns with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to banks to help them further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing the two-year plan to integrate climate risk considerations into the banking supervisory process. Climate risk management is now a standing item on the agenda of prudential supervisory meetings held with bank management. Banking supervisors have also adopted an enhanced CAMEL rating system¹ that incorporates climate risk factors to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of implementing the two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, the HKMA revised the "green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, in order to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address climate risks.  Under the 2023 two-year plan, following the conclusion of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual, the HKMA launched a thematic review of climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. The thematic review covered four major areas, including the governance structure for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and institutional culture, awareness and communication. The HKMA made a number of enhancements to the climate risk stress testing framework, including the introduction of a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impacts on banks of the simultaneous occurrence of economic and climate change shocks. Following these enhancements, and as part of the HKMA's regular supervisor-led stress testing exercises, the second round of the climate risk stress test was launched in June to conduct a comprehensive assessment of banks' climate risk exposures and to further enhance banks' capabilities in managing climate risks. A total of 44 banks participated in this risk stress test, an increase of over 60% compared with the first pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also held a Climate Risk Stress Test Forum in November, which was attended by as many as 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating the exchange of experience among banks, this event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk quantification. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks' progress in implementing module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual. The HKMA held meetings with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and the common challenges faced by the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other publicly available information to assess their progress in this regard. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks, encouraging and supporting them in continuing to strengthen their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's supervisory expectations.  As global attention on climate change grows and efforts to address the issue intensify, the HKMA has noted an increasing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering related products to meet customer needs. In light of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks' sale of green and sustainable investment products, and issued a circular in November setting out the standards the HKMA expects banks to meet and sharing the good practices observed. This circular covered a number of areas, including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training and record-keeping, with the aim of mitigating potential greenwashing risks and enhancing investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments.  The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analytics, enhancing banks' ability to manage climate risks. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot version of a cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technological solutions can assist in conducting physical risk assessments. On the other hand, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, in order to reduce the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform, fully automating the process of collecting financial crime risk data, thereby enhancing banks' workflows for submitting AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the HKMA organised the "Green Fintech Competition", which aimed to seek market-ready solutions to help the banking industry address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted more than 85 submissions from around 70 companies in total. In December, the HKMA held the "Green and Sustainable Banking Conference", providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the roles of low-carbon technology and green fintech in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and the Mainland, and announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition" at the same event. This event attracted around 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulators and academia.  To enhance transparency across financial markets and to promote greater consistency in green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA developed a local green taxonomy framework with the assistance of a consultancy firm. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Prototype of a Green Classification Framework for Hong Kong", seeking stakeholders' views on establishing and implementing a green taxonomy catalogue. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the framework prototype and identifying other areas for the next stage of the framework's development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force, which has identified environmental crimes as predicate offences for money laundering; and in view of the interconnectedness between AML and environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations, this area is receiving increasing attention from more regulators.  The HKMA is keenly aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing monitoring work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, and has incorporated analysis of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. Through its active participation in the scenario design and analysis workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped to further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participates in analysing the interplay between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. In terms of research work, the HKMA has undertaken a number of applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial industry and the economy. Research topics include the climate risk exposures of the banking industry and investment funds², ESG fund flows³, the impact of climate change on property prices⁴, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance in global supply chains⁵. The above research findings have deepened the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, helping to inform the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, this research helps strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shares its research findings with a wide range of stakeholders through international events on climate-related matters and various channels such as the HKMA Research Memorandum.  The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. In accordance with the NGFS's recommendations, the HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, the HKMA helps to promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws lessons from it to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to jointly build a richer ecosystem and promote the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategy. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to support Hong Kong in seizing the opportunities in sustainable finance, with major workstreams including sustainability disclosure, strengthening the ecosystem, transition finance and green fintech. Specifically, a working group on sustainability disclosure has been established to formulate a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. This roadmap will cover four key areas, including sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, as well as skills training. In addition, a transition finance working group has been established to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group has also strengthened the building of the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. In particular, on the data front, we continued to promote the use of the climate and environmental risk questionnaire for non-listed companies launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in the green and sustainable finance field and enhance Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region and globally.
