In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to seize the investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To facilitate the industry's skills training, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the Government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme", providing subsidies to practitioners, students and graduates who receive green and sustainable finance-related training and obtain relevant qualifications. As at December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training or qualifications were registered as eligible training or qualifications under the scheme, and more than 560 subsidy applications were approved. The HKMA also launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module at the foundation level under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners. This module aims to promote talent development in the banking sector and enhance practitioners' overall professional competence. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking industry to develop the professional level of the module to meet the rapidly growing demand of the industry for green and sustainable finance professionals. To help financial institutions and corporates, especially SMEs, better understand key climate and sustainability-related topics, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and transition planning, during the year the HKMA, together with relevant policy bureaux and departments of the Government, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), organised a series of seminars and thematic workshops, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. On the student front, following the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Initiative" in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns' and university bachelor's degree graduates' understanding of sustainable finance. The HKMA is well aware of the potential of technology in filling climate-related data gaps and enhancing data quality, and is therefore committed to making relevant data more accessible and improving data quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group rolled out a series of website enhancement measures to provide financial institutions, corporates and the public with a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information. Key enhancements included an electronic platform for sustainability disclosure, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, as well as more focused, easy-to-browse and searchable data and resources. During "Hong Kong Green Week", the Steering Group also joined hands with Cyberport and Invest Hong Kong to co-organise the "Harnessing Technology to Catalyse Sustainable Finance" event, showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week — Finance Theme" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia and consulting firms. The highlight of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum" co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together more than 400 guests, including top decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. This two-day event explored a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industries, the circular economy, the future development of sustainable finance, and new climate technologies in the emerging and developing markets of the Asia-Pacific region. The forum was supported by public and private sector organisations, which co-organised more than 10 roundtables, seminars and other exchange activities. Topics covered climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomy and green development financing in the "Belt and Road" region. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund co-organised the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" on 29 February 2024 to explore key measures to scale up climate finance, as well as the roles of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. The above activities form part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as a useful platform to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks", serving as a collaboration platform bringing together financial institutions, banking industry associations, research institutions and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held a total of 22 training events and roundtables, attracting more than 7,300 participants from around the world, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, together with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second frontier-topic research report titled "Developing an Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategy: Case Studies". During the year, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established "Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment" (CASI) and the "Green Investment and Finance Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the "Belt and Road" Initiative Green Development International Coalition. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will help facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more funds towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong chapter, which will help support the net-zero efforts of local and Mainland financial institutions. The HKMA assists GFANZ's work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. The HKMA assists in the issuance of green bonds under the programme. To date, the Government has issued about US$25 billion equivalent of green institutional and retail bonds, with the proceeds raised allocated to more than 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the programme, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report", setting out in detail the allocation of proceeds raised from the green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. In the 2023-24 financial year, the Government continued its regular issuance of green institutional bonds and issued about US$6 billion equivalent of green bonds in June. This triple-currency issuance covered US dollar, euro and renminbi bonds of various tenors, attracting different types of investors and receiving an enthusiastic subscription response, with subscriptions reaching close to US$30 billion equivalent. Among them, the size of the renminbi bond issuance increased from RMB10 billion issued in January to RMB15 billion, and a 10-year renminbi bond was introduced for the first time, which helps extend the Government's renminbi yield curve and further enrich the range of offshore renminbi products. The enthusiastic response of global investors to the Government's green bond issuance reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued a second batch of green retail bonds totalling HK$20 billion, further promoting market development and advancing financial inclusion. This issuance offered members of the public an investment opportunity with stable returns, enabling them to both participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a pivotal role in advancing the development of green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has led the way in green and sustainable asset investment, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights and integrating environmental, social and governance factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term value creation thereafter"1, believing that giving full attention to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to become a signatory to the "Principles for Responsible Investment" (PRI) and to set a "Net Zero by 2050" target2 for its "investment portfolio", the HKMA is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasising sustainability—particularly the pressing issue of climate change—with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and pursuing more favourable risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry practice standards, and promoting the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and among central banks. Through stewardship and collaborative measures, the HKMA is committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. Exhibit 1 The Responsible Investment Journey of the Exchange Fund. Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is essential for integrating sustainability and for planning a credible climate transition to achieve net zero targets. To fulfil its commitment to supporting the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) Glasgow Declaration3 and the strategic plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA leads by example by preparing this chapter on the responsible investment of the Exchange Fund in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overriding guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practise responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors the relevant implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investing Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Exhibit 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, convenes semi-annually to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures across the HKMA's various functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. Exhibit 2 The Responsible Investment Governance Structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Exhibit 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, with the initial focus on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainability rapidly evolved and, beyond risk considerations, became a strategic priority for major institutions around the world, the Exchange Fund Investment Office revisited its responsible investment approach. July 2023 marked another milestone, when the Exchange Fund Investment Office established a new Business Strategy division led by the Chief Strategy Officer, responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, and incorporating the dedicated responsible investment team—now known as the Sustainable Investing Team—which was previously under the Risk Management and Surveillance division. This strategic realignment reflects the HKMA's elevation of the focus of responsible investment from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related matters in investment. The Sustainable Investing Team works closely with various teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors, and assists the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the ESG—particularly climate-related—risks and opportunities across various types of investments: Public Market Investments—The Credit, Compliance and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the input of the Sustainable Investing Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reporting from the Risk Management and Surveillance division. In addition, the Sustainable Investing Team also participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring processes of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (please refer to the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 40 for details). Private Market Investments—The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the Private Markets Investment and Risk Management teams for each investment proposal. The HKMA understands that the physical and transition risks4 posed by climate change, as well as the related opportunities, will affect the long-term performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investments. The Emissions Gap Report 20235 published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that, unless further reductions in greenhouse gas emissions are made around the world, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The pressing need for more aggressive policies, technological development or behavioural changes to limit the temperature rise may intensify transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded asset shocks. At the same time, extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and severe, posing additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG factors. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the Exchange Fund's "investment portfolio" to achieve net zero emissions by or before 2050, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged efforts, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The following sections will elaborate on the relevant approaches. Exhibit 3 The HKMA's Three Balanced Measures for Responsible Investment. In progressing towards the net zero target, the HKMA prefers to proactively engage rather than to exclude or divest from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the primary investment objective of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize the opportunity to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess outstanding technology and good corporate governance to respond to the evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emitting industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not help resolve the carbon emissions problem. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries through deploying strategic capital and actively exercising ownership rights, driving them to implement a transition towards sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about beneficial changes for themselves and the world at large. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net zero investment strategy, adopting a comprehensive approach to pursue transition outcomes that align with the net zero targets of the Exchange Fund and the world, while adhering to its guiding principles of responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to promote climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio (Exhibit 4). The HKMA's responsible investment maintained good momentum in 2023. In the public markets, the HKMA launched a brand-new actively managed global equity portfolio themed on sustainability and climate transition, managed by external investment managers, and expanded the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to another asset portfolio managed by external investment managers. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds that the HKMA prioritised for investment outperformed the investment benchmark, demonstrating the philosophy of "doing well by doing good". In the private markets, the HKMA has actively built a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities that are expected to benefit from long-term economic development trends such as the climate and energy transition. For example, during the year the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, reflecting the HKMA's commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs. Exhibit 4 Continuing to Implement Measures to Promote ESG Investment. The HKMA has invested in a company that specialises in producing environmentally friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste (including organic matter such as food waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on energy-intensive high-temperature environments to produce plastics, this company pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This plastic material, made 100% from waste, can serve as a substitute for oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and consumer durables, offering a sustainable and versatile option. At the same time, this plastic material is also compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is a firm supporter of the circular economy. In 2017 and 2019 respectively, the HKMA made two tranches of investment commitments of US$1 billion each to the MCPP, and further collaborated with the IFC to create in 2021 a brand-new global climate-related investment platform, "MCPP One Planet"—the world's first cross-sector emerging-market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP programme, the HKMA has committed to providing loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors—including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate and manufacturing—in 38 developing countries. The IFC has collected data on the MCPP loans. The green and sustainable finance ecosystem is the cornerstone of future global sustainable development. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organisation, adopting a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also places emphasis on the physical and mental well-being of its staff and on social responsibility, and strives to advance financial inclusion and enhance the public's financial knowledge. As a responsible organisation, the HKMA has set sustainability goals under three pillars, namely the environment, staff, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee)¹, established in October and chaired by the HKMA's Chief Executive, is the principal decision-making body for the organisation's various sustainability initiatives. The Steering Committee, formerly the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategy, and policies for corporate sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and regularly submits progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Team provide support in coordinating the organisation's sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming ideas on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The HKMA has drawn up a roadmap to guide its transition path. The focus of the work is to implement carbon reduction strategies in its daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green mobility, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools, and more environmentally friendly modes of operation, reducing waste, and building a culture of sustainability. The HKMA also plans to apply embedded carbon tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, while using carbon offsetting measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. In addition to the aforementioned environmental commitments concerning its daily operations, the HKMA continues to roll out more environmentally friendly operational solutions for the wider community, covering channels applicable to banks for submitting electronic documents and for communication, as well as electronic payment and coin collection programmes for use by the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capacity, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool, and places emphasis on the physical and mental well-being of its staff. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages its staff to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers using social enterprises in its procurement; promotes financial services consumer education; and works with the banking industry to ensure fair access to basic banking services for all sectors of society. The remainder of this chapter sets out the details of the above strategies. Under the HKMA's overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee², chaired by the HKMA's Chief Executive, considers the potential risks and threats that the HKMA faces in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts brought about by climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by more extreme weather, may affect the HKMA's offices and hinder staff travel. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plan to cope with extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. Various measures have also been incorporated into the design of the offices to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy use, air travel, and waste disposal. The HKMA has been monitoring the transition risks it bears by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate goal is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions for Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) across all areas of the organisation's operations by 2050 or earlier. As a near-term emission reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing vehicles to electric vehicles; and, using 2015 as the baseline year, to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various carbon reduction and offsetting strategies. Despite the challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will still adopt a multi-pronged approach to the extent practicable to minimise Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions (such as paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were formulated with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology, which has also been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emissions, energy and paper consumption, and waste data⁶ disclosed in this report. The scope and basis of the verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the Annual Report 2022, the HKMA also, for the first time, independently published the Sustainability Report 2022. The HKMA's efforts to strengthen ESG reporting have been recognised, winning the ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulator to win an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for meeting good ESG standards, noting that the Sustainability Report is clear and easy to read, and that its appointment of an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflects its commitment to high-transparency and accountable reporting. In addition, the HKMA also received the highest rating, the Gold Award in the "Non-Profit-Making and Charitable Organisations" category, in the Hong Kong Management Association's "Best Annual Reports Awards 2023". The judging panel commended the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making good use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's determination to enhance financial knowledge and promote financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impacts caused by its operations, and its internal Green Office Guidelines provide staff with guidance on resource use and the generation of office waste. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of the offices it owns and leases. When renovating offices, existing furniture and renovation materials are reused as far as possible to reduce waste, and environmentally friendly building and decoration materials are given priority. The HKMA has consistently followed this practice, and as a result, in 2021 and 2022 respectively, parts of its offices that completed renovation at Two International Finance Centre were awarded Gold certification under LEED⁷ and the "BEAM Plus Interiors" assessment⁸. Adopting new technologies and making good use of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency remains one of the HKMA's key areas of focus. In addition to promoting good habits, such as switching off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include the use of light-emitting diode (LED) lighting, motion sensors, setting air-conditioning room temperatures at appropriate levels, and making good use of energy in the information technology network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has continued to decrease, standing at 2.59 megawatt-hours per person in 2023⁹, a decrease of 29.7% from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions mainly come from the greenhouse gas emissions caused by the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO2e per person¹⁰, a decrease of 45.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, the HKMA also adopts digital tools and technologies, and automates and streamlines work processes, to build a digital working environment and enhance online collaboration within the organisation.¹¹ Paperless meetings have become the HKMA's primary mode of holding meetings. To further reduce paper consumption and enhance efficiency, various internal administrative matters primarily adopt electronic processes. In addition, the HKMA encourages staff to embrace green and digital working modes, replacing paper documents and communications with digital means. At the same time, work on implementing an electronic records management system is also underway. The above green and digital measures have brought about positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kilograms per person, a significant decrease of 64.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). As most international events resumed being held in physical form following the COVID-19 pandemic, and at the same time to facilitate the development of Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, it was inevitable that the relevant HKMA staff needed to travel overseas on business. To reduce the carbon emissions caused by air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to take direct flights where feasible or to combine different business trips when participating in overseas events. At the organisational level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO2e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA also participated in a "Gold Standard"¹² certified carbon offsetting programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions caused by air travel; the programme carries out waste-to-energy conversion, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement process takes sustainability and environmental considerations into account. As part of a comprehensive review of the organisation's procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of procuring green products has been formalised into an established system, and complies with the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. In addition, the tender assessment criteria have also incorporated ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency. At the same time, all suppliers are required to commit to complying with environmental regulations. In accordance with the "4R" principle, namely Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimise waste generation and manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. A breakdown of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, is set out in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA directly participated for the first time in the red packet recycling programme organised by the management company of the International Finance Centre office building. Staff handed in a total of about 3,000 used but still intact and new red packets. These red packets were subsequently handed over to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use during the following year's Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operational and backup data centres account for a major part of the organisation's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)¹³. In 2023, the HKMA's two data centres were awarded "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under the assessment guidelines "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres" issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organisation in Hong Kong to receive such ratings. Improving the energy efficiency of the two data centres has always been a key area of focus for the technical team. To this end, the team adopted green design in the renovation works and applied energy-efficient good working practices to lower the PUE and achieve the relevant targets, including 24-hour monitoring of the data centres' environmental facilities and the continuous enhancement of environmental factors such as air flow and temperature settings. As the technical team continued to improve the energy use of the data centres, the HKMA appointed an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green level of the data centres and to formulate recommendations to further enhance performance in various aspects. The relevant study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the study was completed, the HKMA also began preparations to qualify for the "Green Data Centre" certification under the "BEAM Plus" certification scheme. The certification process is very comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technical team rolled out optimisation measures in accordance with the recommendations of the consultant's report, enhancing energy performance as well as the health elements of the working environment within the data centres.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the 2023 environmental data ("2023 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The 2023 Data include the total energy consumption in 2023, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), their respective densities, and the changes in these data compared with the 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 Data also include the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared with the level at the time when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol") jointly issued by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, and also covers the relevant data used for annual performance comparison for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 (except for food waste). The verification scope covers a total of 5 office and warehouse assets, of which 4 offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is located at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 5 assets. This verification was carried out in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information", issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to enable the formation of an opinion and conclusion at a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was set in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking, and conducted reliability testing. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant original data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work is entirely independent and impartial. The verification team of the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency was not involved in the preparation process of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data are substantially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu-yan, Audit Supervisor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024.

The threats posed by climate change are imminent, making it all the more urgent to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record, and also the first year in which global temperatures exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. At the same time, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased somewhat during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current measures to mitigate climate change. In the process of addressing global warming, the materialisation of climate-related risks is set to intensify, with impacts on the economy and financial markets that are difficult to predict. Moreover, the current tense geopolitical situation, the increasingly fragmented global economic landscape, the potential aggravation of energy security concerns, coupled with an uncertain economic outlook, all pose greater challenges for countries in addressing climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Across the globe, Asia in particular faces the most severe transition challenges. As the World Economic Forum has pointed out, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth, but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a critical role in whether the world can smoothly achieve the goal of net-zero emissions. As Asia's leading international financial centre, Hong Kong needs to strengthen its leading role and make full use of the power of finance to support and drive the region's transition. To this end, the HKMA last year published the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda", which sets out our vision and roadmap for gradually integrating the concept of sustainable development into the core of the financial system. On the one hand, our work focuses on enhancing the financial industry's capacity to address climate change-related risks; on the other hand, it focuses on helping the industry seize the related new opportunities. At the same time, we also lead by example and play a leading role. The HKMA's sustainable development work encompasses four major areas: supporting the banking sector's move towards net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and driving more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a critical role in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and Asia, but it also faces considerable risks of its own during the transition process. In the "Action Agenda", we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or before, and net-zero emissions in their financing activities by 2050 or before. At the same time, we require all banks to strengthen their disclosure of risks and opportunities related to climate change. While continuously enhancing banks' climate risk management, we also provide guidance for banks' transition planning to help them enhance their capacity to respond to the transition and better manage the related risks. We are also carrying out preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to promote the alignment of Hong Kong's sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with a view to further enhancing the industry's transparency in the related activities. In addition, we are refining the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched in May last year to incorporate more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We hope that, by providing clear criteria, we can guide more funds towards sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change brings significant physical and transition risks that may affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investments. But at the same time, it also presents opportunities for the Exchange Fund to grow and drive positive impact. Our experience has proven that investment returns and positive sustainable impact can be reconciled with each other, and there is no conflict between them. In light of this, we are committed to striving to achieve net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or before, and we have pledged in the "Action Agenda" to support Asia's climate transition through the Exchange Fund's investments. At present, sustainable investments already account for more than 10% of the "Investment Portfolio". To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the International Finance Corporation in November last year to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in the Asian region through co-investment. In addition, in September last year we published the first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise asset ownership and adopt good sustainable investment practices. Financing is particularly important for accelerating the region's transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers (including mainland provincial and municipal governments), Hong Kong plays an important role in channelling funds to accelerate the region's transition. The "Action Agenda" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable financing platform, as well as the goal of promoting sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to drive green bond innovation (including the issuance of the world's first batch of multi-currency digital bonds in February last year), to expanding the scope of subsidies under the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" in May last year to cover transition financing instruments, and to the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" launched in November last year, we have been striving to encourage issuers in the region to use Hong Kong's financial platform to raise the funds needed for a decarbonisation transition. To achieve a robust transition, in addition to capital and innovation, we also need an inclusive and easily accessible sustainable development ecosystem for support. This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent information disclosure, as well as industry talent equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, we have pledged in the "Action Agenda" to support the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosure, and to strive to fill the gap in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosure, in particular by providing convenient and easy-to-use climate disclosure templates to promote sustainability disclosure among SMEs. In November last year, we also launched a "Green and Sustainable Finance" professional-level module under the banking industry's professional qualifications framework, in order to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. In addition, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other activities, we have enabled people from all sectors to participate in discussions on sustainable development, thereby promoting cooperation and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with our sustainable development vision. We have pledged in the "Action Agenda" to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or before, which is 20 years earlier than our original commitment. In addition, in accordance with the roadmap promulgated by the Government, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024, and have incorporated low carbon emissions as a screening factor in our procurement process. At the same time, we continue to enhance work efficiency through digitalisation, foster a culture of sustainable development within the organisation, and inspire staff to actively participate in sustainable development work. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and the drastic changes in the geopolitical situation have added uncertainties to global climate action. However, climate change is an indisputable fact and is gradually intensifying. In the work of addressing climate change, the current situation does not allow us to slacken in the slightest. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help reduce the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system, and bring us opportunities along the way. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, striving to advance our sustainable development work and deepening our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the severe challenges we face, we will, as always, be committed to supporting the building of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia, and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the present generation. As an international financial centre and a hub for sustainable finance in the Asian region, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and around the world. In October 2024, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), which sets out the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timeline within which we are committed to achieving various goals, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance the relevant efforts. The HKMA plans to strengthen the resilience of Hong Kong's financial industry and the HKMA itself in addressing climate change risks, and to promote the transition of the Asian region towards a more sustainable economy, through the formulation of strategic policies, the enhancement of regulatory engagement, and the improvement of internal operations. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA is also committed to leveraging its influence and taking part in the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during their transition to net-zero emissions. Our priority work in 2025 includes: - Launching a new round of thematic examinations on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting a third round of consultation meetings, to review banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant supervisory requirements and to further strengthen banks' climate risk management capabilities; - Refining the work of incorporating climate risk stress testing into the HKMA's supervisor-driven stress testing framework; - Continuing to advance the work of incorporating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; - Commencing preparatory work on formulating relevant supervisory requirements for implementing, in the local banking sector, the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks to be issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards); - Completing the preparation of the new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual, which provides banks with guidance on transition planning; and - Sharing with the industry good practices on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to its role as a banking regulator, the HKMA also plays the role of a facilitator, committed to promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in providing financing for the transition. We have published the first phase of the "Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance", which provides the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitates the relevant financing. The HKMA has commenced the second phase of the taxonomy work to expand its coverage, including adding transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate change adaptation objectives. In addition, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will hold another green fintech event in 2025 to encourage banks' adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well positioned to support the demand for sustainable financing in the region. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme", whose expanded coverage will include sustainable projects, such as social responsibility projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and set an example for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable funds. We will also strengthen our promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions and enterprises from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing subsidies to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme". Although there is increasing market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures by institutions and enterprises, different entities vary in their capabilities and levels of readiness in making sustainability disclosures, and some entities may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to work with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their customers with more comprehensive climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how to leverage technology to further make existing resources more convenient and easy to use; and collaborate with major local industry organisations to provide the training needed by the industry. The sustainable finance market is ever-changing and requires expanding the local talent pool and filling the knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. The HKMA's key work in 2025 includes collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training courses for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework", and identifying areas where the industry has further training needs through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030" study. In addition, we plan to work with key stakeholders to strengthen the promotion of the Government-funded "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Training Programme" and to review the scope of application of the programme. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks" to launch dedicated initiatives in the Asian region, including conducting green finance research, providing insightful market analysis, offering targeted upskilling and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps to make green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, in support of the transition of the overall economy. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can promote positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to setting an example in institutional sustainability. In line with the accelerated net-zero commitment timeline announced in the "Action Agenda", the HKMA will progressively incorporate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment and reporting at a pragmatic pace, and continue to advance institutional sustainability. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on material issues. In addition, we will also conduct energy audits and use technology solutions to assess the material impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, so as to enhance our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the "Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap" published by the Government, and are actively carrying out preparatory work to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects in accordance with the principles of energy efficiency and energy conservation. We will also expand digital measures to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and enhancing the overall digital experience for our staff, banks and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, a banking regulator, a market facilitator, a responsible investor and a sustainability-focused organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework that leads the formulation of its relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of relevant measures, and ensures that sustainability considerations are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and working practices. In its commitment to good corporate governance, the HKMA has put in place a robust sustainability governance framework for its sustainability-related work, featuring clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. This governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively incorporated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability work. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: - the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which are responsible for monitoring the HKMA's work, including its sustainability efforts, and for making recommendations; - the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and policies at the management level; - in relation to responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - in relation to other functional areas, the relevant teams and working groups, which are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government bureaux, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's various sustainability initiatives over the past years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 to serve as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas. The Steering Committee is responsible for: - providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of banking, the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; - overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; - assessing the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG targets; and - overseeing the external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. In addition, we invite the Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainability matters to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on the major outcomes of their work and their future plans. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, the Corporate Development and Operations Department, the External Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC co-initiated the Steering Group in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts in relation to the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been committed to strengthening the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system to climate risks, while also contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their day-to-day business operations, and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system by channelling funds towards green and sustainable projects. As the regulator of the banking sector, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" ("Action Agenda"), setting out the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance hub and to support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The "Action Agenda" comprises eight major goals across four areas. To help the industry achieve the objectives of the relevant banking policies, we have been carrying out the following work. All banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or before, and net-zero emissions in their financed activities by 2050 or before. All banks to enhance the transparency of climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices in transition planning with the industry, and launched an industry consultation on the draft of Module GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to respond to the net-zero transition and on the related risk management. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating into the assessment process the relevant factors put forward by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) for effectively managing climate-related financial risks, and of encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management framework (including transition planning) in responding to climate risks. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the "Action Agenda". In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (Taxonomy) to address the industry's concerns about greenwashing and to help channel funds towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four industries, and aims to be interoperable with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating elements tailored to local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope covered by the Taxonomy, and are consulting a broad range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable funds. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management, and was committed to supporting banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to respond to climate change. The HKMA also completed all the work of the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to incorporate climate risk into the banking supervisory process. To promote banks' capacity in strengthening climate risk management, the HKMA shared with the banking industry the good practices observed in thematic examinations and consultation meetings, mainly including: - Establishing a robust governance structure that clearly sets out the responsibilities of the board and senior management. - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters: (1) promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategy; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA held a Balanced Supervision Roundtable on the theme of climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on a number of climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning and transition finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing, and helped inform the HKMA's work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA launched a round of thematic examinations of banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, and assessed their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The thematic examinations covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing Module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual, and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest supervisory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing. We provided feedback and guidance based on the specific circumstances of the banks to support their climate risk management efforts. In 2024, the HKMA completed the second round of the banking sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST), with a total of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups participating. The results showed that under various scenarios (including a hypothetical scenario in which climate risks and a macroeconomic downturn occur simultaneously), the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience in withstanding severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report setting out the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. The HKMA understands that banks encounter numerous challenges relating to data and methodology in climate risk management, and has therefore been committed to a number of initiatives to promote the application of technology in addressing these challenges. To address the problem of the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for conducting climate risk assessments, the HKMA launched the Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on Hong Kong's residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform based on user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA collaborated with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the financial services industry as a whole. During the year, we published an application practice guide and two "Regtech Use Case Booklets" (in English), setting out technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessment, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also held the third "FiNETech", bringing together more than 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration. The HKMA is keenly aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing monitoring work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, and has incorporated analysis of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, assisting central banks and supervisors in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth vintage of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Transition Plans Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participated in analysing the interaction between the transition planning of financial and non-financial firms and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the "Practical Guidance for Banks on the Use of Green Technology" (in English), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change on the financial industry and the economy as a whole. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in withstanding monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on the direction of foreign direct investment, and the role of the financial industry in the transition to a low-carbon economy. These research findings not only deepened our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, helping to inform the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, this research helped strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings were also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels such as international forums and the HKMA Research Memorandum. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), which is responsible for research work under the Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provided evidence that low-emission firms can derive significant benefits from carbon pricing, and highlighted its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study was featured in the HKIMR's "Insights from Monetary Research", and was shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA's Liquidity Facilities Framework is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, we help promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draw on the insights gained to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA's Sustainable Finance Action Plan (Action Plan), the HKMA is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to developing Hong Kong into a preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and beyond, supporting technological innovation in the green segment of financial markets, enhancing sustainability disclosures in the industry, and expanding the local green talent pool while addressing the knowledge gap in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Developing Hong Kong into a preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally; catalysing sustainable finance innovation; supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures; and addressing the talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region. To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing a total of about US$28 billion equivalent in green bonds, sold to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of the green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the Programme and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope of the Programme was expanded to cover sustainable projects and renamed the Government Sustainable Bond Programme (Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes the Green Bond Report annually, detailing the allocation of the proceeds raised from the green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing about US$3 billion equivalent in institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This triple-currency issuance covered bonds of various tenors denominated in renminbi, US dollars, and euros. These bonds attracted the participation of different types of investors, with an enthusiastic subscription response, recording subscription amounts of over US$15 billion equivalent. Among them, the 20-year and 30-year renminbi green bonds were issued by the Government for the first time and represent the longest-tenor renminbi bonds issued by the Government to date, providing a new benchmark for the market and further demonstrating the exemplary role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the choice of offshore renminbi investment products in Hong Kong. In addition, the enthusiastic response of global investors to the green bonds issued by the Government reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers in the region to raise sustainable development funds using Hong Kong's financing platform, the HKMA continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme launched in May 2021, which provides subsidies to eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The Scheme has been well received by the industry, and as at the end of 2024, the Scheme had granted subsidies to about 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total value of over US$140 billion. The Scheme was extended by three years to 2027 in May 2024, and the scope of subsidies was expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the Scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to use Hong Kong's transition financing platform to gradually reduce carbon emissions. - Granted subsidies to about 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total value of over US$140 billion (as at the end of 2024) - Extended by three years to 2027, and the scope of subsidies expanded to cover transition financing instruments. Meanwhile, the HKMA has actively promoted Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, and this work has achieved satisfactory results. Among these, in August, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time, with a total value of RMB7 billion, including RMB2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB0.9 billion in social responsibility bonds. In September, the People's Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, with a total value of RMB5 billion, including RMB1.5 billion in green bonds.
