In October, the People's Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, with a total value of RMB3 billion, including RMB1 billion in blue bonds and RMB1 billion in sustainable bonds. The above issuance activities once again highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and other parts of the world. With the various measures above, Hong Kong has been able to consolidate its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, in 2024 Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub in Asia for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds, with the total value of such bonds arranged through Hong Kong reaching US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two batches of landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, being the world's first tokenised government green bonds and the world's first multi-currency digital bonds respectively. These issuances demonstrate the Government's support for market participants in the region applying asset digitalisation and innovative technology in the green and sustainable finance space. The HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovative development in Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market. The working group on sustainability disclosure under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) has been working on Hong Kong's adoption of the International Financial Reporting Standards - Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards). In December 2024, the Government released the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong, providing a clear pathway for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to provide support to entities at different stages of preparedness to achieve high-quality sustainability disclosures, making sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. It is worth mentioning that we continued to encourage the use of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Unlisted Companies (Questionnaire), which was launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template that facilitates sustainability disclosures by enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to facilitate online completion by enterprises (see the QR code below). The HKMA is enhancing the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, with specific measures including selecting core questions from the Questionnaire and providing common use scenarios for the Questionnaire. In addition, we are also striving to improve the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The HKMA leads by example, making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains rich content on the HKMA's climate-related operational risks, as well as its plans and implementation progress for achieving climate targets. For details of the sustainability disclosures on our own operations, please refer to the chapter "A Sustainable HKMA". Given the rapidly changing sustainable finance market, and to address the knowledge and talent gaps, the HKMA is strengthening skills training work in the banking industry and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA, together with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the Foundation Level of the Green and Sustainable Finance module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners in July 2023. The module aims to help banking industry professionals acquire green and sustainable finance knowledge and develop related professional competencies in a more effective manner, and covers four main areas of work: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainability/climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainability strategy, compliance and controls. In addition, the Professional Level of the Green and Sustainable Finance module, targeting middle and senior banking practitioners responsible for related work, was also launched in November. To provide the necessary training for banking practitioners, HKIB, as the administering body of the Green and Sustainable Finance module, launched the Foundation Level training course of the module in May. Following the launch of the Professional Level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking industry in 2025 to develop the Professional Level training course. To understand the banking industry's further skills and training needs, the HKMA is currently working with the banking industry to conduct the "Future Banking Talent for 2026 to 2030" study, with the aim of publishing the study results in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the "Future Banking Talent for 2021 to 2025" paper published in June 2020. The results of the follow-up study will provide an important reference for the industry, helping it to formulate and adjust talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking industry. The HKMA also continues to assist in implementing the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Training Scheme through its collaboration with the Steering Group, subsidising practitioners, graduates, and students to receive sustainable finance-related training. As at December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses had been registered as eligible training courses under the Scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025-26 Budget that the Scheme would be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions centred on the global sustainable finance market, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. In addition, the HKMA supported the establishment of a chapter of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen skills training work in transition planning and transition finance.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can complement each other, the HKMA adheres to the philosophy of responsible investment in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritising sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership. Investing prudently in accordance with the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term value enhancement", the HKMA believes that giving full consideration to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate the associated investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a firm signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment work. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and striving for more desirable long-term risk-adjusted returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment tools to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1).  The HKMA leverages its role as a major investor to contribute to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document available to investment partners through its annual ESG workshops and the HKMA website. We partner with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry practices and standards, and to promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and the central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future in which finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced its "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), setting out its aim to achieve net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and to mobilise partners to support the low-carbon economic transition, thereby further reinforcing its commitment to investing in a sustainable future.  The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The foremost guiding principle establishes the tone that the HKMA can practise responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors the relevant implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategist, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and joined by the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Strategist of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures of the HKMA's various functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to fulfil the HKMA's overall ESG objectives.  The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams of the Exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors, and assists the senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the ESG, and particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities of various investments: - Public Market Investments – The Credit, Regulatory and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the situation after ESG factors have been integrated into credit risk models with reference to the views of the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team also participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring process of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (for details, please refer to the "Promoting Active Ownership" section under the "Risk Management" section on page 39). - Private Market Investments – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the Private Markets Investment and Risk Management teams on each investment proposal.  The HKMA understands that the physical and transition risks brought about by climate change, as well as the associated opportunities, will affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund's investments. The "Emissions Gap Report 2024" published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that, unless there is large-scale global mobilisation to rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties in policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may intensify transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the rising frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional risks of physical damage and financial loss to investments. Amid these challenges, as governments and industries turn towards sustainable solutions, this also creates potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure.  The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. The HKMA has set the target of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and continues to advance its work through an orderly three-pronged approach to achieve this target (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the "Action Agenda", which reinforced the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the low-carbon economic transition, the HKMA is inclined to proactively engage in dialogue rather than to exclude or divest from investable assets.  Investing in a Sustainable Future Exchange Fund "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier - Actively expanding the scope and variety of sustainable investments, particularly climate-transition-themed investments in the public and private markets - Integrating ESG factors into every investment decision, with particular attention to climate change and transition prospects - Formulating clear ESG expectations that align with international standards and best practices, and requiring all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to comply with them - Committing to reduce the Weighted Average Carbon Intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from 2017 levels by 2030 or earlier  Supporting Regional Transition through Investment - Continuing to engage with external investment managers to optimise investment opportunities that drive transition - Continuing to identify and prioritise quality investment opportunities that can facilitate Asia's transition and bring positive impact globally  First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio plays a key role in achieving the primary investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA is able to seize opportunities to invest in enterprises that are undergoing transition and possess outstanding technology and good corporate governance to address the ever-changing global climate trends, including enterprises in high-emission industries.  Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding the relevant investments or divesting does not help resolve the carbon emissions problem. On the contrary, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, driving them to transition to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about beneficial change both for themselves and for the world as a whole. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, so as to drive full decarbonisation of the economy as a whole.  As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of an asset portfolio depends not only on the portfolio's own adjustments, but also on a broad-based economic transition. Although there is no perfect single solution, in 2024 the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategy, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the net-zero targets of the Exchange Fund and the world. The strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, decarbonisation tilting of the asset portfolio, and thematic investments in various assets aligned with net-zero pathways. In the public markets, this may involve tilting the asset portfolio towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, coupled with stewardship to drive corporate transition. In the private markets, there may be greater emphasis on transition-enabling investments. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can facilitate climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio.  Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund "Investment Portfolio", with financial performance comparable to the relevant asset portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public Market Investments – The HKMA launched an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continued to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide competitive returns while funding sustainable projects (for a related case study, see the "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds" section). - Private Market Investments – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. The HKMA also leverages its extensive network and expertise to actively identify and assess investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through establishing strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (for related examples, see the "Joining Forces to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond" section).  - Passive portfolios that use ESG indices as investment benchmarks - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios whose benchmarks are non-ESG indices - Governance-themed active portfolios - Sustainability- and climate-transition-themed active ESG portfolios - Projects with sustainability characteristics, such as renewable energy infrastructure and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed on energy transition and decarbonisation across the globe, Asia and the Global South - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Programme (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on investing in sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" programme, which provides Paris Agreement-aligned climate-related investments in emerging markets  The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a quasi-governmental entity. The proceeds raised from the green bond were allocated to a number of projects, including upgrading the ageing equipment of several sewage treatment facilities. These upgrade projects covered the optimisation of monitoring and control systems and pump performance, so as to generate positive environmental benefits in wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling processes. In addition to continuously treating wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recycling rate of up to 100%. These facilities also use the gas generated during the sludge treatment process to power boilers and generate electricity.  The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond provided funding for a number of projects, including the rehabilitation of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is intended to divert excess water flow from rivers to arid areas. The primary purpose of the project was to rehabilitate the increasingly deteriorating canal lining, so as to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency and reclaim flooded areas. In addition, the project provided skills training for local stakeholders, promoting the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies such as micro-irrigation as well as sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the HKMA's key priorities in fulfilling this commitment in 2024 was the plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, which is 20 years earlier than the original target, in line with the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda". In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering staff training and well-being, and to advancing financial inclusion and enhancing the public's financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for the organisation's various sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 the HKMA's new target of achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations by 2030, as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"). At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) provides guidance on the implementation of sustainability measures relating to corporate operations, staff well-being, and social connection, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, communicating, and reporting on the organisation's sustainability measures. The Green Office Focus Group and the Volunteer Service Team, comprising staff from various operating departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former is a platform for brainstorming and putting forward suggestions on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its staff, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for 18 consecutive years, from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to adopt a structure comprising three pillars: Environment, Staff, and Social Responsibility. - Focusing on decarbonisation and digitalisation of the HKMA's daily operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 - Adopting green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promoting more environmentally friendly practices to the financial industry and society at large - Building a proactive workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives - Fostering a working environment that promotes collaboration and caring inclusiveness, valuing diversity, and enhancing staff sense of belonging - Providing a quality working environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle - Cultivating a culture of caring for society - Incorporating social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promoting financial inclusion and enhancing the public's financial literacy through consumer education activities. The HKMA is mindful of climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its own corporate operations to 2030, 20 years earlier than its original commitment, as part of the "Action Agenda". The HKMA has revised its roadmap towards net-zero transition, with a focus on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations, concentrating on cutting carbon emissions, conserving energy, minimising paper use, and recycling waste, while making full use of improvements by local power companies in their fuel mix for electricity generation. In addition, the HKMA has established a digitalised working environment to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, the HKMA understands the importance of cultivating a culture of sustainability, and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under the overriding 2030 net-zero emissions target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and to procure with low carbon wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel and participation in carbon offset programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offset programmes to cover all remaining major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its actual operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market's low-carbon transition, from introducing electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and collecting coins for recirculation into the market. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection efforts, as well as promoting staff well-being and caring for society. Under the HKMA's overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the design of the HKMA's offices incorporates a range of measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fire, and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures covering not only its offices but also its communications and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA has also been monitoring the transition risks it faces by tracking greenhouse gas emissions from its own operations, waste generation, as well as energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions relating to its corporate operations by 2030. These targets were developed with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA uses the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's main greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions arising from the consumption of fossil fuels to generate electricity. As data for individual suppliers is not available, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate its main Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfill and staff air travel and commuting. The detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and basis of the Agency's verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" appended at the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, upholding the same climate-related standards it expects of the banks it regulates and the financial system it supervises. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024, and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve full green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in its various renovation works in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and decoration materials or traded in old items for a discount on new ones, thereby reducing waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews the energy consumption and energy-saving measures of its offices and data centre, and in its 2024 data centre facility upgrade project adopted a modular-design uninterruptible power supply system, further optimising the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency at partial loads, and features advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. Through the digital workplace, the HKMA has enhanced internal virtual collaboration and, together with streamlined workflows, has effectively reduced paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the service life of mobile and desktop devices by referring to the manufacturers' software update cycles, which prolongs the secure usage period of the devices. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the "4R" principle, namely refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has placed recycling bins for different materials at various convenient locations in its offices. To improve recycling rates, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit netting bags in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending its collected food waste to a waste-to-energy centre in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Less Waste at Events" pledge, committing to take measures to reduce the waste generated by its various events. The HKMA continues to give priority to procuring goods that meet the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their trips carefully, for example by combining multiple journeys when attending overseas events. At the organisational level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing its annual air travel carbon emissions by about 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in a Gold Standard-certified carbon offset programme to offset its remaining air travel carbon emissions; the programme focuses on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as talks and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance staff understanding of environmental sustainability issues. The HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month" from Earth Day on 22 April 2024 throughout the month of May, with the theme "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This was a good opportunity for the HKMA to promote its commitment and momentum in practising environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The activities included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" encouraging staff to practise green living, a "Save the Earth" quiz game, and a "Kokedama" indoor plant care workshop originating from Japan; results of the waste audit were also shared, and a community recycling centre operator introduced best practices for recycling. To sustain the momentum of the "Green Month", the HKMA launched a recycling campaign of about six months in October, highlighting the responsible handling of waste and reminding staff that pooling together small changes in individual habits can greatly enhance the organisation's overall recycling performance. One of the highlights of the campaign was the launch of a "Green Move" video, in which several senior officials shared recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders to remind staff to take practical action to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff questionnaire survey to understand their awareness of sustainability and to gather their views on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help formulate future sustainability training activities and waste handling strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as an important agent of change, and is therefore committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition and driving the financial industry and society as a whole to adopt sustainable practices. The HKMA has introduced a number of measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the "Common Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the HKMA extended the platform's service scope in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The purpose of expanding the platform's service scope was to further simplify the submission process for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new measures introduced in 2024 included the SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA questionnaires through a simplified submission process, and the Smart Information and Document Management System, a central platform that provides users with advanced search functions for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted independent verification of the environmental data ("the Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel for 2024, as well as their respective intensities. In addition, the Data includes Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions for 2023 and 2024 generated from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting, together with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data is compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol") jointly issued by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, of which 5 offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is located at 6) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance of the accuracy and reliability of the Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification exercise was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and draw a conclusion in order to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to its source, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking, and performed reliability testing. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA was responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - the Data is materially accurate and reliable; - the HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shum Siu-yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025
